acquisition_note: Organisation egress policy blocked all direct HTTP fetches to journalism/data/government hosts (403 at CONNECT). WebSearch (routed via Anthropic, not the egress proxy) was the only available channel to current market information. Each record carries the source URL as published by the search index; snippets are as returned. Primary-source verification remains outstanding for every record.

signals.title: ITV unveils drama slate for rest of 2026
signals.claim: ITV recommissioned Trigger Point for a fourth series with Vicky McClure returning as bomb-disposal officer Lana Washington.

signals.title: ITV drama slate 2026
signals.claim: The Dark, a four-part serial written by Chris Dunlop, stars Suranne Jones as DI Monica Kennedy investigating a murder she believes begins a wider campaign.

signals.title: ITV drama slate 2026

signals.conflict_note: Two sources give different casts and origins for 'The Blame' (Jodie Comer/Paapa Essiedu original vs Michelle Keegan/Douglas Booth adapted from Charlotte Langley novel). Unresolved.

signals.title: ITV drama slate 2026
signals.claim: Adultery, a six-part drama by Danny Brocklehurst led by Dominic Cooper and Romola Garai, follows two ordinary families disrupted by an affair.

signals.title: ITV drama slate 2026
signals.claim: Professor T returns for a fourth season; Van Der Valk returns for a new three-episode block with Marc Warren.

signals.title: ITV drama slate 2026
signals.claim: Red Eye returns with Jing Lusi as DS Hana Li, guest star Martin Compston, Lesley Sharp as Head of MI5 and Jemma Moore as journalist.

signals.title: Secret Service (2026 TV series)
signals.claim: Secret Service, a British espionage series commissioned by ITVX from Potboiler Productions and All3Media, premiered 27 April 2026.

signals.title: Upcoming British TV Series for 2026

signals.title: Upcoming British TV Series for 2026
signals.claim: Channel 4's Maya is a psychological thriller about a mother and daughter placed in witness protection in a remote Scottish village.

signals.title: BBC commissioning activity 2026
signals.claim: BBC commissioned period drama 1536, adapted from Ava Pickett's award-winning play, as an eight-part series.

signals.title: BBC commissioning activity 2026
signals.claim: BBC commissioned political thriller D-Notice from writers Adam Patterson and Declan Lawn.

signals.title: Line of Duty returns for series seven
signals.claim: A new six-part Line of Duty by Jed Mercurio, produced by World Productions with ITV Studios for BBC iPlayer and BBC One, starts filming in Belfast Spring 2026.

signals.title: Mammoth Screen slate
signals.claim: Mammoth Screen is producing lunar thriller First Woman for ITV, supernatural drama The Witch Farm for BBC, Code of Silence series two for ITV, and Agatha Christie's Endless Night for BBC/BritBox.

signals.title: Bad Wolf 2026 productions
signals.claim: New seasons of Industry (HBO/BBC) and Red Eye (ITV) launched in 2026; The Other Bennet Sister (BBC/BritBox) set for release later in the year; Damson Idris to star in and executive produce The Lords' Day; Colin Firth cast in an untitled Apple TV drama.

signals.title: 2026 productions shooting in UK and Ireland
signals.claim: The Lords' Day, a Netflix series adapted from Michael Dobbs's novel about a siege at the Houses of Parliament, produced by Bad Wolf, was in production from August in London.

signals.title: Legends (2026 TV series)
signals.claim: Legends is a British crime thriller created by Neil Forsyth, released on Netflix 7 May 2026, starring Steve Coogan, Tom Burke and Hayley Squires, following customs officers in a top-secret operation.

signals.title: Unchosen
signals.claim: Unchosen is a British psychological thriller created and written by Julie Gearey, released on Netflix 21 April 2026.

signals.title: New British Netflix series 2026-2027
signals.claim: A new Harlan Coben adaptation scripted by Danny Brocklehurst, with Minnie Driver and Ruth Jones, continues Netflix's UK trend of releasing Coben series on New Year's Day.

signals.title: Sky Up Next 2026
signals.claim: Meantime, a Sky Original comic crime thriller from Frankie Boyle and Neil Webster based on Boyle's debut novel, starring James McAvoy, has started production.

signals.title: Sky Up Next 2026
signals.claim: Sky announced the return of Mr Bigstuff for a third series and Gangs of London for a fourth.

signals.title: Sky Up Next 2026
signals.claim: The Good Daughter, an adaptation of Karin Slaughter's novel starring Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy, arrives in 2026.

signals.title: 5 commissions Last Resort (w/t) from Pernel Media
signals.claim: Channel 5 commissioned new drama series Last Resort (w/t) from Pernel Media starring Caroline Quentin, Tessa Peake-Jones, Jason Watkins and John Hannah.

signals.title: Madame Blanc Mysteries returns for fifth series
signals.claim: The Madame Blanc Mysteries returns to Channel 5 for a fifth series.

signals.title: Channel 5 drama slate
signals.claim: The Good Ship Murder returns for a fourth series, produced by Clapperboard in association with FIFTH SEASON.

signals.title: Channel 5 commissions first true crime drama Maxine
signals.claim: Channel 5 commissioned its first true crime drama, Maxine, from Clapperboard.

signals.title: 5 commissions factual drama To Nicola, Love Peter (w/t)
signals.claim: Channel 5 commissioned major new factual drama To Nicola, Love Peter (w/t).

signals.title: C5 reveals six new drama commissions
signals.claim: Channel 5 announced six new drama commissions for the 2025-2026 season spanning thrillers, cosy crime, family drama and at least one French co-production, as part of a stated ambition to become a pre-eminent source of British drama.
signals.strategic: Channel 5 expanding scripted volume against a contracting market

signals.title: Channel 5 factual
signals.claim: Channel 5 recommissioned The Accused from Brinkworth Productions, 12x90' across two years.

signals.title: Blue Lights Series 4
signals.claim: Blue Lights, the Northern Irish police procedural created by Declan Lawn and Adam Patterson, returns for series four on BBC One in autumn 2026.

signals.title: Top-tier dramas returning in 2026
signals.claim: Doctor Foster, Sherwood, The Night Manager, Line of Duty, Peaky Blinders and Rivals are among returning titles in 2026.

signals.title: Renewed shows 2026
signals.claim: Jimmy McGovern's drama set in a young offenders institution returns for a third season with David Tennant leading as Prison Officer Bailey.

signals.title: TRUE CRIME channel expands original slate
signals.claim: TRUE CRIME channel commissioned UK Forensic Breakthroughs and Deadly Destinations, premiering autumn 2026; Deadly Destinations explores real crime cases linked to travel.

signals.title: Inspector Ellis a streaming sleeper hit
signals.claim: A new two-part British crime series, Inspector Ellis, emerged as a major streaming sleeper hit on Acorn TV in July 2026.

signals.title: A Taste for Murder
signals.claim: A Taste for Murder, a British crime drama for ITVX and BritBox, began streaming 7 April 2026.

signals.title: Official BFI statistics 2025
signals.claim: UK film and high-end TV production spend reached £6.8bn in 2025, up 22% year on year; HETV accounted for £4bn and film £2.8bn.

signals.title: Official BFI statistics 2025
signals.claim: Inward-investment film and HETV delivered £5.8bn, 85% of total UK production spend, while UK domestic HETV spend was £688m, 17% of total HETV spend.
signals.interpretation: Domestic commissioning is a small minority of UK production activity

signals.title: BFI H1 2026 figures
signals.claim: Overall UK film and high-end TV production spend fell 16.6% in H1 2026.

signals.title: BFI H1 2026 figures
signals.claim: Inward TV production spend decreased 23.5% from £1.7bn in the equivalent 2025 period; inward investment accounted for 78% of UK HETV spend in H1 2026, totalling £1.3bn from 39 programmes.

signals.title: BFI H1 2026 figures
signals.claim: 37 UK domestic productions accounted for 45% of programmes in H1 2026 with UK production spend of £337m, an increase from £332.3m in the equivalent 2025 period.
signals.interpretation: Domestic production is flat-to-slightly-up while inward investment collapses — domestic share of programme count is rising

signals.title: UK feature production spend drops 6% H1 2026
signals.claim: Total UK feature production spend dropped 6% in H1 2026, but local films and co-productions enjoyed boosts.

signals.title: British TV co-productions plummeted
signals.claim: Spending on co-productions was £19.6m in 2024, less than half the £44.2m in 2023 and nearly 60% down on 2022's £48.3m.

signals.title: British TV co-productions plummeted
signals.claim: There was a 22% drop in domestic high-end television commissions in 2024 alongside a 50% decrease in international co-productions.

signals.title: British TV co-productions plummeted
signals.claim: Spending on domestic shows fell 25% from £797.7m in 2023 to £598.2m in 2024, the lowest domestic spending since 2020.

signals.title: UK TV dramatists lament austerity era
signals.claim: Producers described a greenlight from a UK broadcaster on a major drama as effectively meaningless because broadcasters can provide only around a third of the financing required to start production; UK broadcasters no longer have capacity to plug the gap when international investors cut back.
signals.interpretation: The binding constraint on UK drama is deficit financing, not commissioning appetite

signals.title: BBC boss held crunch talks over scripted funding crisis
signals.claim: BBC Director-General Tim Davie held crunch talks with top producers over the UK scripted funding crisis.

signals.title: Limited series production companies 2026
signals.claim: Blumhouse Television produces limited series at 30-50% below Tier 1 pricing using lower budgets, genre-specific programming (horror, psychological thriller) and brand identity strong enough to act as a commissioning signal, attracting multiple platform deals in 2025-2026.
signals.interpretation: Low-budget genre specialisation is functioning as a commissioning advantage

signals.title: Film production budget guide 2026
signals.claim: Commercially successful low-budget productions tend to be tightly contained: limited locations, small casts, minimal VFX, short shooting schedules, leaning into strong genre concepts (horror, thriller, contained drama).

signals.title: The three budget buckets running TV in 2026
signals.claim: With buyers consolidating and leverage shifting to platforms, making programming for less is no longer optional but essential.

signals.title: Limited series commissioning priorities
signals.claim: Netflix is commissioning limited series with built-in global audience signals: IP with pre-existing fanbases (literary adaptations, true crime events, recognisable franchise extensions) and genre content with proven multi-territory performance (thriller, crime, historical drama).
signals.interpretation: Pre-existing IP is a commissioning precondition, disadvantaging original spec material

signals.title: Screen Ireland TV Drama Production funding
signals.claim: Screen Ireland offers TV drama production funding with a maximum award of €650,000-€950,000 depending on total budget, for Irish producers with prior international marketplace finance and substantial broadcaster or streaming funding.

signals.title: Northern Ireland Screen four-year strategy
signals.claim: Northern Ireland Screen's 2026-30 strategy includes establishing an all-island co-funding mechanism with Screen Ireland and a cash-flowing tax credit, addressing producer demand for streamlined cross-border working.
signals.interpretation: A new financing route opening precisely as the co-production market collapses

signals.title: Screen Ireland 2026 production slate
signals.claim: Screen Ireland launched a 2026 production slate of 87 projects for audiences and the international market.

signals.title: Ofcom Media Nations 2026
signals.claim: Netflix is first choice for 26% of UK viewers against the BBC's 25%, published 29 July 2026.

signals.title: UK SVOD plateau
signals.claim: UK households with an SVOD service reached 70% in Q1 2026, only two percentage points above 2021; Netflix is in 61% of UK households, Amazon Prime Video 46%, Disney+ 26%.
signals.interpretation: Subscriber growth is exhausted; platforms must compete on retention, which favours returnable series

signals.title: Ofcom Media Nations 2026
signals.claim: SVOD revenues rose 18% year on year to £5.17bn in 2025, driven by hybrid monetisation including ad-supported tiers; broadcaster on-demand content grew 9% year on year.

signals.title: ITVX biggest ever month
signals.claim: ITVX surpassed 400 million monthly streams for the first time, recording 468 million streams and 21 million users in June 2026, up 173 million streams year on year.

signals.title: ITVX passes one billion streams for 2026
signals.claim: Gone became the most watched drama on any UK channel or streaming platform, reaching 5.5 million viewers and 23.8 million streams.

signals.title: ITVX May 2026 performance
signals.claim: Believe Me became ITVX's most watched drama in over a year on first seven days of availability, with 58% of the audience watching every episode in the first week; Secret Service reached 13 million streams for its five episodes.
signals.interpretation: True-crime-adjacent limited series delivering exceptional completion rates

signals.title: ITVX top titles 2026
signals.claim: Top-performing ITVX titles include Vera, Believe Me, The Family Next Door, Cape Rock Killer and The Affair; Love Island remains the top title overall with streaming accounting for 64% of its audience.

signals.title: ITVX soap streaming
signals.claim: Coronation Street and Emmerdale together generated more than 54 million streams with viewing up more than 40%.

signals.title: Post-Peak TV Crunch
signals.claim: Ampere Analysis found only 2% fewer Western European scripted commissions announced in 2025 than in 2020, but they take on average 40% longer to make; the bottleneck is production speed, not commissioning decline. Presented by research manager Olivia Deane at Series Mania, March 2026.
signals.interpretation: Scarcity is in production-ready, fast-to-make material rather than in commissioning appetite

signals.title: Post-Peak TV Crunch
signals.claim: Asked to name their favourite genre globally, consumers put crime and thriller top at 11% while romance came last at 6%; yet romance was the only genre with positive acquisition growth 2024 to 2025, up 18%.
signals.interpretation: Audience preference and buyer acquisition behaviour are diverging

signals.title: Post-Peak TV Crunch
signals.claim: The supply crunch in Western Europe and North America opened the door for Asia Pacific content, which in 2025 overtook both regions in scripted non-original acquisitions premiering globally.
signals.interpretation: Western supply shortfall is being filled by APAC acquisitions rather than by new Western commissions

signals.title: Streamers shift towards scripted romance
signals.claim: Scripted titles accounted for 83% of first-run romance commissions in H1 2026; romance became the second most-commissioned scripted genre globally, and the most-commissioned in Latin America at 30% of scripted commissions.

signals.title: Ampere on scripted romance
signals.claim: Literary adaptations accounted for more than 40% of scripted romance commissions since H1 2025; the volume of first-run book adaptations rose 73% between the 12-month periods covering H2 2023-H1 2024 and H2 2025-H1 2026.
signals.interpretation: Buyers are de-risking through pre-existing IP, which structurally disadvantages original spec screenplays

signals.title: Streamers favouring scripted romance
signals.claim: In Q1 2026, 49% of respondents aged 18-24 said they enjoyed romance, seven percentage points above the global average across all ages.

signals.title: BBC commissioned half of all UK scripted
signals.claim: Ampere found the BBC greenlit 129 of 256 UK scripted shows in 2023; UK scripted commissions fell 18%; within BBC commissions crime and thriller titles were up 16%, kids up 23%, comedy down 27%.

signals.title: UK scripted content drops
signals.claim: Streamer commissions in the UK dipped 20% to 49, commercial free-to-air rivals nearly halved to 54, and pay-TV outfits such as Sky fell from 52 to 27.

signals.title: True Crime & Investigation 2026
signals.claim: Ampere reports true crime was 16% of all documentary commissions worldwide in 2025, up from 15%, with 632 new crime documentary commissions tracked across 22 major media markets; UK and US remain dominant, with BBC and Channel 5 the top UK commissioners in 2025.

signals.title: True crime commissioning maturing
signals.claim: Trade reporting notes the frenzy of true crime commissioning has matured, with one production executive describing a fall from nine of twelve simultaneous true-crime productions to three of eight.
signals.interpretation: True crime supply is contracting from peak even as it remains the largest documentary subgenre

signals.title: Sharp drop in Nordic commissioning
signals.claim: In the Nordic region unscripted commissions fell 21% and scripted 30% from 2024 to 2025; more broadly there has been a 25% decrease in scripted commissioning since the peak of TV around 2022.

signals.title: LatAm scripted decline
signals.claim: Overall scripted TV commissions in Latin America declined 13% between H1 2025 and H1 2026, while unscripted contracted at twice that rate, falling 26%.

signals.title: International TV taking safe bets on procedurals
signals.claim: Buyers are looking for lighter and upbeat content rather than very dark programmes, with cosy crime and procedurals in demand rather than expensive auteur-driven dramas; police procedurals, reboots and low-cost entertainment are in demand as networks focus on the bottom line over audience growth.
signals.interpretation: Direct buyer-stated preference against dark auteur drama and toward contained, warm, repeatable formats

signals.title: Mipcom refrain
signals.claim: Streamers are seeking content skewing towards older viewers and are less interested in chasing young adult audiences, because grown-ups are the ones who pay for subscriptions.
signals.interpretation: Older-skewing audience is a stated buyer priority, contradicting the youth-focused assumption

signals.title: South Korean drama commissions shrink
signals.claim: South Korean drama commissions are shrinking despite global demand.

signals.title: Short-form serials gaining viewers
signals.claim: In-app revenue for micro-series content is forecast at US$3.8bn in 2025, with Deloitte predicting revenue will more than double to US$7.8bn in 2026.
signals.interpretation: The fastest-growing scripted revenue pool identified anywhere in this corpus

signals.title: Short-form serials empowering independent studios
signals.claim: Global revenue from micro-drama apps surged from US$178m in Q1 2024 to nearly US$700m in Q1 2025; short-form serials are empowering independent studios.
signals.interpretation: Deloitte explicitly identifies independent studios, not incumbents, as beneficiaries

signals.title: DramaBox
signals.claim: DramaBox averaged 44 million monthly active users during H1 2025, with $323m revenue and $10m net profit in 2024.

signals.title: ReelShort
signals.claim: ReelShort took approximately $400m revenue in 2024, with its user base rising from 40 million to 50 million between October 2024 and May 2025.

signals.title: Vertical drama explained
signals.claim: Vertical drama is mobile-first storytelling filmed in 9:16 with episodes of 60 to 90 seconds, some extending to three minutes.
signals.interpretation: Format is radically cheaper and faster to produce than high-end TV

signals.title: Vertical series producer guide 2026
signals.claim: In the US, Peacock licensed 10 micro dramas from ReelShort and planned Bravo original micro dramas for summer 2026.
signals.interpretation: Mainstream US broadcasters are now licensing micro-drama, legitimising the format

signals.title: UK vertical drama indie KIN launches
signals.claim: KIN, a UK vertical drama indie founded by Ben Sedley, Ben Clapp and Kate Arton, brings together experience across advertising, filmmaking and documentary to create original scripted content designed specifically for mobile viewing.
signals.interpretation: First-mover UK indie in vertical drama — the UK market is only now forming

signals.title: Vertical Dramas: From Micro to Macro
signals.claim: The RTS is running an event on vertical dramas as a new area of scripted entertainment, covering commercial models and how the genre evolves as established players increase their interest.
signals.interpretation: UK industry establishment is actively convening on the format — early institutional attention

signals.title: London TV Screenings 2026 takeaways
signals.claim: London TV Screenings 2026 takeaways included startling facts about microdramas and Asia taking centre stage.

signals.title: Microdramas drive new growth
signals.claim: Ampere identifies microdramas as driving new growth in the Latin American scripted market even as overall scripted commissions decline 13%.
signals.interpretation: Microdrama growth is occurring inside otherwise contracting scripted markets

signals.title: ITV Studios acquires Eagle Eye Drama
signals.claim: Eagle Eye Drama, the independent scripted producer behind Professor T, Hotel Portofino and The Couple Next Door, sold a majority stake to ITV Studios in April 2026.
signals.interpretation: Consolidation reduces the number of independent buyers of writer material

signals.title: Bad Wolf production chief heads to Mammoth Screen
signals.claim: Bad Wolf's production chief moved to Mammoth Screen as production boss.

signals.title: Intergenerational divides as a mechanism of class inequality in UK television drama
signals.claim: UK television drama is undergoing rapid change with increasingly risk-averse commissioning, more precarious employment and more geographically dispersed production, raising questions about who gets to make television and whose lives are treated as credible on screen.

signals.title: What's On? A report on class inequality in UK TV drama
signals.claim: Social class remains one of the most persistent and least resolved inequalities in UK television; unlike race, gender or disability it is not a protected characteristic, and working-class origin remains largely invisible and unaccountable in recruitment and commissioning decisions. Research conducted in partnership with the BBC and Channel 4.
signals.interpretation: Both major public-service buyers are formally engaged with a finding that working-class life is under-represented on screen

signals.title: Working-class talent fights to survive a contracting UK screen industry
signals.claim: Large broadcasters including the BBC and Channel 4 remain central to commissioning, but decision timelines and development fees have not adjusted to the financial reality facing freelancers and small companies.

signals.title: BBC Writers Open Call
signals.claim: The BBC Writers Open Call accepts unsolicited scripts to identify and nurture writing talent, open to writers new to the BBC and those with theatre or radio experience; the window is short, with a stated deadline of noon on 2 December 2025.

signals.title: Channel 4 New Writers Scheme
signals.claim: Over nine months writers receive support to complete a spec script plus industry training, mentoring and introductions to scripted drama production companies; targeted at emerging writers from the Nations and Regions, welcoming writers near Channel 4's Bristol, Glasgow and Leeds hubs and this year Northern Ireland.
signals.interpretation: Explicitly regionally targeted — geography is a qualifying advantage, not a disadvantage

signals.title: 4Screenwriting
signals.claim: 4Screenwriting requires writers to attend two weekends in London and write at least two drafts of an original one-hour television drama between January and June 2026.

signals.title: How ideas are pitched to Netflix
signals.claim: Netflix accepts submissions only through a licensed literary agent or from a producer, attorney, manager or executive with a pre-existing relationship; anything else is unsolicited and cannot be accepted.

signals.title: Coverfly is shutting down
signals.claim: Coverfly shut down on 1 August 2025 along with The Tracking Board, ScreenCraft, The Script Lab and WeScreenplay, removing the largest free aggregation layer between unrepresented writers and the industry.

signals.title: Black List pricing 2026
signals.claim: The Black List charges $30 per month hosting and $100 per feature evaluation; a six-month run with two evaluations costs about $380 per script.
signals.interpretation: Route cost scales linearly per script, penalising volume strategies

signals.title: InkTip screenwriter services
signals.claim: InkTip Pro costs $32.50 per month including script listings and the Weekly Pitch newsletter; standalone script listings are $19.99 per month; free for qualified filmmakers to search.

signals.title: Nicholl Fellowships 2025-2026
signals.claim: Up to five $35,000 Nicholl Fellowships are awarded annually; as of the 2024 contest 24 winning scripts had later been produced.

signals.title: Book Adaptation Rights Market 2026
signals.claim: The 11th Book Adaptation Rights Market runs 4-6 September 2026, with growing demand from producers looking for original intellectual property and repeat participation from publishers.
signals.interpretation: Producers are actively sourcing IP through rights markets rather than spec screenplays

signals.title: Netflix options over 25 books
signals.claim: Netflix optioned over 25 books for TV series and film development for 2026 and beyond.
signals.interpretation: Netflix's development pipeline is being filled from published IP rather than spec scripts

signals.title: Book to film and TV adaptations
signals.claim: More books than ever are being optioned due to demand from streaming services, with Netflix saying the chance of a book being adapted has never been higher; books are increasingly optioned at the same time publishers acquire them, with companies willing to take risks on early drafts.
signals.interpretation: Buyers will take a risk on an unfinished book but not on an unrepresented screenplay — a route asymmetry
